title: Frequency-addressed modal cell: the field as compressed computational matter
summary: This pass records a cross-family synthesis that only became explicit after the resonance, field-computing, computational-matter, NSSN and structural-compiler lines were viewed together. Earlier projects mostly chose a wave/field substrate and asked what it could compute. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell reverses that direction: start from an already-interesting resonant, state-dependent receiver and ask what smaller operator description survives compression. v0 shows that state compression is not mechanism compression: rank-8 POD captures 99.86% of a 36-state teacher while naive nonlinear closure fails autonomous rollout. v1 extends the object through branching axonal matter with deliberately weak local ephaptic timing. v2 shows frozen branching collapses exactly to a sparse fixed-delay graph; only runtime-dependent timing survives that attacker. v3 then imports one useful abstraction from wetware computing without importing organoid biology: hide the substrate internals and learn a stimulation language through sparse external ports. FANMC learns a robust four-symbol persistent code, but a linear state-space reservoir nearly matches it; space alone is perfect, frequency alone still carries a weaker one-port code, and phase alone falls near chance. The resulting wall lesson is narrower and stronger: computational matter should be judged by what externally controllable operator survives ordinary reduced, graph, reservoir and address-ablation attackers.

nodes.claim: Tests whether rich receiving/transmitting matter can be compressed and externally programmed through sparse stimulation ports, while preserving only the runtime-dependent computation that survives reduced-state, graph, reservoir and address-ablation attackers.
nodes.survived: v0 establishes strong state compressibility (rank-8 POD energy 0.998602). v1 adds grown branching axonal routes and weak local coactivity-dependent timing. v2 isolates the static-graph boundary. v3 hides the population internals behind eight stimulation/recording ports and learns a four-symbol external write/read code: full FANMC reaches 1.000 held-out accuracy after a 96-step wait, while removing the slow material write falls to 0.1875. With one electrode fixed, frequency-only writes retain 0.8125 accuracy; frequency+phase reaches 0.9167.
nodes.killed: v0's naive nonlinear modal closure fails autonomous held-out rollout. v2 kills any claim that branching geometry alone is a new primitive because the frozen arbor is exactly reducible to a sparse fixed-delay graph. v3 kills a first architecture-advantage claim: a 48-state linear state-space reservoir reaches 0.9792 through the identical black-box interface, and spatial-only FANMC reaches 1.000, so frequency is not necessary for the easiest four-symbol task. Phase-only addressing is 0.2708, near four-class chance. The result is a programming/interface mechanism, not superiority to conventional recurrent state.

edges.why: The new repository explicitly builds its teacher from the NotSoSimpleNeuron quasi-active frequency gate plus the later synthetic local voltage-dependent interaction, then asks whether those resident state-conditioned dynamics admit a much smaller autonomous modal surrogate.

Entrain already made frequency an executable routing coordinate and measured its Arnold-tongue resolution limit. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell keeps frequency/phase as the probe address but changes the scientific direction from constructing oscillator matter to reducing an existing richer receiver.

InformationFlow demonstrated WHERE/WHICH/SIGN selection through spatial overlap, frequency and phase but supplied its useful nonlinear coupling explicitly. The new reduction experiment asks whether useful state-dependent coupling can instead be extracted from richer computational matter rather than written into the field law by hand.

Operaattori shows the forward reduction idea on real morphology: complicated physical structure can compile to compact transport and nonlinear operator objects. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell applies the analogous compression question to a resonant state-dependent synthetic receiver, without claiming direct ancestry or that the v0 teacher is Operaattori's biological model.

v3 turns the substrate into a hidden machine that can only be programmed by choosing interventions and reading consequences. That is the same active-identification grammar AnotherOddThing isolates, now applied to discovering a reusable stimulation code rather than selecting among explicit hypotheses.

ReadWrite studies what a bounded observer can reveal by applying known writes. v3 makes that constraint the programming interface itself: internal FANMC state is hidden, and only sparse port-level stimulation plus later readout is legal.

motifs.title: The field is no longer the hypothesis; it is a reduced representation of computational matter
motifs.description: Earlier field and oscillator projects usually started by choosing a field law and exploring the computation it could support. Operaattori, NotSoSimpleNeuron and FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell point in the reverse direction: begin with a richer physical or synthetic receiver, identify what operator family it actually implements, and try to compress that family into a smaller executable object. The v0 failure sharpens the rule: a compact state manifold is not enough; the reduced law must remain causal and stable when run autonomously on interventions it did not fit.

motifs.title: Frequency can address a resident operator, but filtering alone is not enough
motifs.description: SpectralNeuron establishes the boring floor: resonance supplies finite FDM-style addressing. Entrain adds measured entrainment routing and phase relations. InformationFlow uses frequency/phase/spatial overlap to select a nonlinear write. NotSoSimpleNeuron then shows the stronger receiver-side object: active resident state changes cross-mode coupling and the operator encountered by the next event. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell asks whether that stronger object can be compressed while keeping frequency/phase as the external address rather than confusing a band-pass filter with the computation itself.

motifs.title: A compressed representation earns mechanism status only when it survives new interventions
motifs.description: MatrixInMatrix already separates a compact harmonic reconstruction from the source dynamics that heal and evolve. NeuralAlgorithmDecoding requires an executable causal surrogate rather than a pretty hidden geometry. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell makes the same boundary dynamical: rank-8 coordinates explain almost all sampled state variance, yet a locally better nonlinear transition fit fails when autonomously rolled through unseen frequencies, tone pairs and histories. Representation compression and mechanism compression are different gates.

motifs.title: Frozen structure can collapse to a graph; runtime-dependent matter is the surviving residue
motifs.description: The axonal extension creates a useful correction to the structure-as-computation story. Development can manufacture a branching route, but once that geometry is frozen and conduction is context-free, a sparse graph with fixed delays reproduces terminal arrival timing exactly. What survives the attacker is not branching itself but the weak dependence of propagation timing on nearby co-active axonal matter. This keeps the claim narrow: physical structure may determine the operator, while runtime material state determines whether the operator is richer than a static graph representation.

motifs.title: Do not program hidden matter by writing its internals; learn an external intervention language
motifs.description: The FinalSpark wetware-computing interface motivates a useful abstraction even after the biology is removed: internal parameters may be inaccessible while the substrate remains controllable through a small set of stimulation/recording ports. FANMC v3 implements that constraint synthetically. A controller learns a write/read code only from externally observed consequences. The slow-state ablation establishes that persistent FANMC writes need resident hidden state, but the linear-reservoir attacker shows the interface itself is not uniquely biological. Address ablations further separate coordinates: space is strongest here; frequency alone remains a usable one-port address; phase alone does not.
